# Make your own Lienzo extension

The "Make your own" walkthrough from Help, step by step, with a complete example. The full contract is in [extensions.md](extensions.md).

## Overview

Ask your agent for a tool, try it, and share it. No build step.

An extension is a small tool that joins Lienzo: one HTML page that reads the Lienzo, changes the selection and, with your permission, edits the canvas in one undoable step. You do not need to write it yourself: your agent writes it, saves it, and it appears in the + catalog. These pages walk through it from the first request to sharing it in the catalog.

### By hand

1. Ask your agent for the tool (step 1).
2. Read what it saved in Extensions (step 2).
3. Open it from the + catalog and try it on a few cards (step 3).
4. Check what it may do (step 4).
5. Export it or publish it to the catalog (step 5).
6. Let your agent use it too (step 6).

### Ask your agent

- “Make me a Lienzo extension that counts the cards in the selection.”
- “Write a Lienzo tool that turns the selected cards into a checklist.”

## 1. Ask your agent

Say what the tool is for, what it acts on, and what it changes.

Your agent saves extensions with the canvas_catalog tool, which asks for your approval the first time. A good request says three things: what the tool works on (the selection, a Frame, the whole Lienzo), what it shows, and what it changes when you press it.

### By hand

1. Open the conversation where your agent works (in Paseo, the chat next to the Lienzo; on desktop, the agent's own app or terminal).
2. Describe the tool in one or two sentences.
3. Approve the catalog change when your agent asks.

### Ask your agent

- “Make a Lienzo extension called Title Case: it shows how many cards are selected and has one button that rewrites their titles in Title Case.”
- “Write a Lienzo tool that shows the selected Frame's cards as a numbered list I can copy.”
- “Add a page of Help to your extension that explains how to use it.”

### Tips

- Ask for a Help page too: the agent adds a docs field and the tool gets its own page here, under Extensions.
- Name the permission it may need. A tool that only reads and selects needs none.

## 2. What it writes

A manifest and one self-contained page that talks to window.lienzo.

Your agent saves a manifest: an id, a name, a one-line description, an icon, the permissions it asks for, the page (html), and optionally its Help page (docs, short Markdown). The page runs sandboxed in its own frame, with no access to Paseo, your files or other sites. It reaches the canvas only through window.lienzo.

### The parts of the page
- `lienzo.onContext(fn)` calls `fn` with the Lienzo (cards, Frames, links, where each one is), the selection and the theme's colours, now and on every change.
- `lienzo.select(ids)` changes the selection; `lienzo.onSelection(fn)` hears it change; `lienzo.open(id)` selects a card (with **view**, it also flies there).
- A tool that does not need every card's content says so with `context: { document: "outline" }` (or `"none"`) in its manifest, and reads cards whole with `lienzo.read(ids)`: its messages stay small on a big Lienzo.
- `lienzo.edit(operations, label)` changes the canvas in one transaction you can undo. It needs the **edit** permission.
- `lienzo.view` reads and moves the camera (the **view** permission): `get()`, `fit(ids)`, `onChange(fn)` (every frame while the camera moves) and `toScreen(rect)`. Good for a tool that walks the Lienzo like slides.
- `lienzo.keys.bind(keys, fn)` takes arrows, Space, letters and the like while the tool is open; `lienzo.highlight(ids)` outlines cards for a moment, never saved; `lienzo.storage` keeps a small JSON value for this Lienzo.
- `lienzo.kit.stage(...)` draws things with the canvas' own selection, hover and drag behaviour.
- `lienzo.action(name, fn)`, in a script marked `data-lienzo="actions"`, offers a job your agent can run too (step 6).

### The manifest
```json
{
  "id": "title-case",
  "kind": "tool",
  "api": 1,
  "name": "Title Case",
  "description": "Gives the selected cards titles in Title Case.",
  "icon": "CaseSensitive",
  "permissions": [
    "edit"
  ],
  "html": "<p id=\"info\">…</p><script>…</script>",
  "docs": "Title Case gives every selected card…"
}
```

The whole contract is in [docs/extensions.md](https://github.com/Gabsplat/paseo-canvas/blob/master/docs/extensions.md).

## 3. Test it

Open it from the + catalog and try it on a few cards.

A saved extension appears at once in the + catalog under Extensions, in ⌘K, and as a card in the Extensions screen. It opens as a tab of the Properties panel and works on the shared selection, so what you select on the canvas is what it sees.

### By hand

1. Press + in the toolbar and choose your tool under Extensions.
2. Select a few cards: the tool should react at once.
3. Press its button. If it changed the canvas, ⌘Z undoes the whole step.
4. Ask your agent to fix anything that is off; saving the same id replaces the tool.

### Ask your agent

- “The Title Case tool ignores Frames. Make it rename the selected Frames too.”
- “Your tool's text is hard to read in the light theme. Use the theme colours it is given.”

### Tips

- Extensions run in the web and desktop apps, not on the phone.
- If the tool says it has no permission, see step 4.

## 4. Permissions

Reading and selecting are free; changing the canvas, the internet and moving the view are asked for.

An extension declares what it needs: edit (change the canvas), network (load things from the internet) and view (move the canvas camera, for tools that present or tour the Lienzo). Without network it can load nothing from outside its own page. A tool made here by you or your agent holds what it declares. One that arrives in a file or from the catalog holds nothing until you allow it: until then it can only read and select.

### By hand

1. Open Extensions (menu → Extensions).
2. A card that waits shows a warning strip: read what it asks for, then press Allow.
3. Replacing the file with different code asks again.

### Tips

- There is no permission to talk to the agent: the canvas never sends anything to it. You talk to your agent in your own chat.

## 5. Share it

Export one file, or publish it to the catalog with a pull request.

Every extension travels as an extension file (JSON). Export saves one tool as its own file: send it to someone and they add it with Add from file…, after a review of what it asks for. To share it with everyone, Publish… checks it, saves the file, and opens GitHub to propose it to the Lienzo extensions catalog. Once the pull request is merged it shows in Discover.

### By hand

1. Open Extensions and find your tool's card.
2. Press Export for a file, or Publish… for the catalog.
3. Publish… checks the tool, saves the file and opens GitHub. Sign in there, add the file, and open the pull request.
4. Add a README.md and a screenshot.png next to extension.json if you like.

### Tips

- Lienzo never holds a GitHub token: everything on GitHub happens in your browser.
- Every id in a file starts with the file's id and a dot, like title-case.title-case.

## 6. Let your agent use it

Give the tool actions, and your agent can run it for you.

An extension can offer actions: named jobs your agent runs itself, like "Title Case these cards". The work is written once, in a script of the page marked data-lienzo="actions". The page's own buttons run it with lienzo.run, and your agent runs it with canvas_extension_run, without the page, in a sandbox on your computer. Each run the agent makes is one step in History, marked (agent), and undoes like any other.

### By hand

1. Ask your agent to add an action to the tool (it declares it in the manifest and registers it in the actions script).
2. Open the tool's Help page: "For your agent" lists its actions.
3. Ask your agent to use it: "Title Case the cards I selected".
4. Check History: the step reads "Title Case (agent): Title Case". Undo brings the old titles back.

### Ask your agent

- “Add a titleCase action to my Title Case extension so you can run it yourself.”
- “Use the Title Case extension on the cards in the Ideas Frame.”

### Tips

- An action that changes the canvas needs the edit permission. One from a file or the catalog cannot edit until you allow it.
- The actions script must not use the page (no document, no buttons): it also runs without one.
- An action runs for at most 2 seconds and 64 MB, without timers or the internet; a failing one changes nothing.

### In the manifest
```json
{
  "actions": [
    {
      "name": "titleCase",
      "description": "Rewrites card titles in Title Case, in one undoable edit. Without ids it works on the cards the person selected.",
      "input": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "ids": {
            "type": "array",
            "items": {
              "type": "string"
            },
            "maxItems": 200,
            "description": "The cards to change. Default: the person's selection."
          }
        }
      },
      "returns": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "changed": {
            "type": "integer",
            "description": "How many titles changed."
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

### In the page
```html
<script data-lienzo="actions">
// The work, once: the button below runs it, and so can an agent (canvas_extension_run), headless, without this page.
function titleCase(t) { return t.replace(/\b\w/g, function (c) { return c.toUpperCase(); }); }
lienzo.action('titleCase', function (input, c) {
  var ids = input.ids || c.selection;
  var ops = c.document.blocks.filter(function (b) { return ids.indexOf(b.id) >= 0 && titleCase(b.title) !== b.title; })
    .slice(0, 200).map(function (b) { return { type: 'block.update', id: b.id, patch: { title: titleCase(b.title) } }; });
  if (!ops.length) return { changed: 0 };
  return lienzo.edit(ops, 'Title Case').then(function () { return { changed: ops.length }; });
});
</script>
```

Headless, the action sees `lienzo.context` (the document and the selection; no theme or layout), `lienzo.edit`, `lienzo.select`, `lienzo.storage`, `lienzo.sleep`, `lienzo.action` and `lienzo.run`. All its edits in one run become one transaction.

## 7. How it appears

A panel, an effect over the canvas, a bubble at the selection, or the whole screen.

An extension chooses how it shows. A panel floats over the canvas, with a title bar, only a close button, or nothing at all. An overlay is a clear layer over the whole canvas, for effects drawn right over the cards; clicks pass through it to the canvas unless it asks for them. A popover is a small bubble that points at what is selected. Fullscreen covers Lienzo, for games and presentations. Your agent can also open a tool for you, in the mode it picks, and hand it what to work on.

### By hand

1. Open the tool from the + catalog or ⌘K: it appears the way it was made to.
2. Esc closes anything but a panel with a title bar; a small ✕ is always there (in a corner, or on the chip at the top for an overlay).
3. While an overlay draws, the chip at the top names it. Its ring turns to the tool's colour while it takes the pointer.

### Ask your agent

- “Make me a tool that turns the selected cards to dust, drawn over the canvas.”
- “Open Snap on the cards in the Ideas Frame.”
- “Save the Snap example from Lienzo Help as an extension.”

### Tips

- Hiding cards for an effect (lienzo.hide) changes nothing that is saved: they come back when the tool closes.
- A tool that came in a file opens without its permissions until you press Allow.
- Snapshots of cards (lienzo.view.snapshot) work in the desktop app; in a browser the tool draws without them.

### In the manifest
```json
{
  "presentation": {
    "mode": "panel",
    "width": 360,
    "height": 420,
    "chrome": "minimal",
    "position": "center",
    "accent": "violet"
  }
}
```

- **mode**: `panel` (the default), `overlay`, `popover` or `fullscreen`.
- **width** 200–720 and **height** 120–900 pixels; other values are clamped. A panel starts at 320 × 440, a popover at 280 × 160.
- **chrome** (panel): `full` (title bar), `minimal` (a ✕ in the corner) or `none` (the page draws everything; a ✕ shows on hover).
- **position** (panel): `right`, `left`, `bottom` or `center`.
- **dimCanvas**: 0 to 0.6, a shade over the canvas under the tool.
- **accent**: `accent`, `success`, `warning`, `violet` or a `#rrggbb` colour, for its icon and title.

### While it runs
- `lienzo.ui.state`: the mode, size, chrome, position, `capturing`, `canSnapshot` and `rect` (where the frame is on the canvas area).
- `lienzo.ui.set({ mode, width, height, chrome, position, dimCanvas })` changes any of them; the page is not reloaded. `lienzo.ui.onChange(fn)` follows them.
- `lienzo.ui.capturePointer(true)` lets an overlay take clicks, `false` gives them back to the canvas.
- `lienzo.hide(ids, { ms })` and `lienzo.show(ids)` hide cards on this screen only. Nothing is saved, and they come back when the tool closes.
- With the view permission, `lienzo.view.get()` has `rects`: where each visible thing is, in the overlay's own pixels; while the camera moves, `lienzo.view.toScreen(context.layout[id])` gives it every frame. `lienzo.view.snapshot(ids)` gives a picture of them (desktop app).
- `lienzo.ui.safeArea` says what Lienzo's own islands cover (the toolbar, the top islands, Properties when open) and `lienzo.ui.freeRect` the largest free rectangle: draw there. With the view permission, `lienzo.ui.immersive(true)` hides Lienzo's UI and goes full screen to present over the real canvas; Esc leaves it.
- `lienzo.input` and `lienzo.onInput(fn)`: what your agent passed when it opened the tool (`canvas_extension_open`).

An overlay is transparent: leave the page's background unset. Its root element carries `data-lienzo-mode="overlay"` for your CSS.

### The Snap example
An overlay that turns the selected cards to dust, then deletes them or brings them back. Its manifest:
```json
{
  "id": "snap",
  "kind": "tool",
  "api": 1,
  "name": "Snap (example)",
  "description": "Example: turns the selected cards to dust over the canvas, then deletes them or brings them back.",
  "icon": "Sparkles",
  "permissions": [
    "view",
    "edit"
  ],
  "presentation": {
    "mode": "overlay",
    "accent": "violet"
  },
  "html": "…the page below…",
  "docs": "…its Help page…"
}
```

Its page:
```html
<style>
html,body{margin:0;height:100%;overflow:hidden;background:transparent;font:13px/1.45 system-ui,-apple-system,"Segoe UI",sans-serif}
canvas{position:fixed;inset:0;width:100%;height:100%;display:block}
.pill,.ask{position:fixed;display:none;border:1px solid;box-shadow:0 10px 30px rgba(0,0,0,.18)}
.pill{left:50%;bottom:92px;transform:translateX(-50%);padding:7px 14px;border-radius:999px;white-space:nowrap}
.ask{width:264px;padding:14px 16px 12px;border-radius:12px}
.ask b{display:block;font-size:14px;margin-bottom:2px}.ask p{margin:0 0 12px;opacity:.75}
.row{display:flex;gap:8px;justify-content:flex-end}
button{font:inherit;font-weight:600;padding:6px 12px;border-radius:8px;border:1px solid;cursor:pointer}
kbd{font:inherit;font-weight:600}
</style>
<canvas id="dust"></canvas>
<div class="pill" id="hint"></div>
<div class="ask" id="ask" role="dialog" aria-label="Snap"><b id="title"></b><p id="text"></p>
<div class="row"><button id="back">Bring back</button><button id="del">Delete</button></div></div>
<script>
var cv = document.getElementById('dust'), g = cv.getContext('2d'), hint = document.getElementById('hint'), ask = document.getElementById('ask');
var back = document.getElementById('back'), del = document.getElementById('del');
var ctx = null, k = null, dust = [], pictures = [], snapped = [], phase = 'idle', t0 = 0, W = 0, H = 0, dpr = 1, at = { x: 0, y: 0 }, pending = null, job = {};
function size() { dpr = window.devicePixelRatio || 1; W = innerWidth; H = innerHeight; cv.width = W * dpr; cv.height = H * dpr; }
addEventListener('resize', size); size();

// Colours from the theme, so it reads in light and dark.
function paint() {
  hint.style.background = ask.style.background = k.surface; hint.style.color = ask.style.color = k.foreground;
  hint.style.borderColor = ask.style.borderColor = k.border;
  back.style.background = 'transparent'; back.style.color = k.foreground; back.style.borderColor = k.border;
  del.style.background = k.accent; del.style.color = k.background; del.style.borderColor = k.accent;
}
function cards(ids) {
  var by = {}; ctx.document.blocks.forEach(function (b) { by[b.id] = b; });
  return ids.filter(function (id) { return by[id]; }).map(function (id) { return by[id]; });
}
function idle() {
  phase = 'idle'; ask.style.display = 'none'; lienzo.ui.capturePointer(false);
  var n = cards(ctx.selection).length;
  hint.innerHTML = n ? 'Press <kbd>Enter</kbd> to snap ' + n + (n === 1 ? ' card' : ' cards') + ' · <kbd>Esc</kbd> closes' : 'Select cards, then press <kbd>Enter</kbd> · <kbd>Esc</kbd> closes';
  hint.style.display = 'block';
}
lienzo.onContext(function (c) {
  ctx = c; k = c.theme.colors; glow = rgb(k.needs); paint();
  if (pending) { var w = pending; pending = null; snap(w); } else if (phase === 'idle') idle();
});
// An agent can open it on given cards: canvas_extension_open { extension: "snap", input: { ids, delete? } }.
lienzo.onInput(function (input) { if (input && input.ids) { if (ctx) snap(input); else pending = input; } });
lienzo.keys.bind('Enter', function () { if (phase === 'idle') snap({}); });

function load(url) { return new Promise(function (ok) { var i = new Image(); i.onload = function () { ok(i); }; i.onerror = function () { ok(null); }; i.src = url; }); }
// A card as Lienzo draws it, when no snapshot can be taken (in a browser): its surface, border, title and summary.
function standIn(o, w, h, b) {
  var fit = function (t, max) { t = String(t || ''); while (t && o.measureText(t).width > max) t = t.slice(0, -2) + '…'; return t; };
  o.beginPath(); o.roundRect(0.5, 0.5, w - 1, h - 1, 8); o.fillStyle = k.surface; o.fill(); o.strokeStyle = k.border; o.lineWidth = 1; o.stroke();
  o.textBaseline = 'top'; o.fillStyle = k.foreground; o.font = '600 14px system-ui,-apple-system,"Segoe UI",sans-serif'; o.fillText(fit(b.title, w - 24), 12, 12);
  var text = b.data && (b.data.summary || b.data.text); if (text && h > 44) { o.fillStyle = k.muted; o.font = '12px system-ui,-apple-system,"Segoe UI",sans-serif'; o.fillText(fit(text, w - 24), 12, 35); }
}
// Every few pixels of a card become one grain: it waits its turn (left to right, a little at random), then drifts off.
function grains(r, img, shot, b) {
  var w = Math.max(1, Math.round(r.width)), h = Math.max(1, Math.round(r.height)), off = document.createElement('canvas'), o = off.getContext('2d');
  off.width = Math.round(w * dpr); off.height = Math.round(h * dpr); o.scale(dpr, dpr);
  if (img && shot) { var sx = img.naturalWidth / shot.width, sy = img.naturalHeight / shot.height; o.drawImage(img, (r.x - shot.x) * sx, (r.y - shot.y) * sy, r.width * sx, r.height * sy, 0, 0, w, h); }
  else standIn(o, w, h, b);
  // The card stays a crisp picture; each grain is cut out of it as it leaves.
  var card = { off: off, o: o, x: r.x, y: r.y, w: w, h: h }; pictures.push(card);
  var px = o.getImageData(0, 0, off.width, off.height).data, s = Math.max(2, Math.round(Math.sqrt(w * h / 3000)));
  for (var y = 0; y < h; y += s) for (var x = 0; x < w; x += s) {
    var i = (Math.min(off.height - 1, Math.round((y + s / 2) * dpr)) * off.width + Math.min(off.width - 1, Math.round((x + s / 2) * dpr))) * 4; if (px[i + 3] < 12) continue;
    // Once it flies, one grain in four glows a little in the canvas' violet, so the dust reads on any card and theme.
    var c = [px[i], px[i + 1], px[i + 2]], f = Math.random() < .25 ? mix(c, glow, .6) : c;
    dust.push({ card: card, lx: x, ly: y, x: r.x + x, y: r.y + y, s: s, out: false, c: 'rgba(' + c[0] + ',' + c[1] + ',' + c[2] + ',', f: 'rgba(' + f[0] + ',' + f[1] + ',' + f[2] + ',', wait: (x / w * .7 + (1 - y / h) * .15 + Math.random() * .3) * 1300,
      vx: 40 + Math.random() * 110, vy: -30 - Math.random() * 80, life: 1 + Math.random() * .9, seed: Math.random() * 6.3 });
  }
}
function rgb(hex) { var m = /^#?([0-9a-f]{6})$/i.exec(String(hex).trim()); var n = m ? parseInt(m[1], 16) : 0x8a6cf0; return [n >> 16, n >> 8 & 255, n & 255]; }
function mix(a, b, t) { return [0, 1, 2].map(function (j) { return Math.round(a[j] + (b[j] - a[j]) * t); }); }
var glow = [138, 108, 240];
function frame(now) {
  var t = now - t0, alive = 0; g.setTransform(dpr, 0, 0, dpr, 0, 0); g.clearRect(0, 0, W, H);
  for (var i = 0; i < dust.length; i++) { var p = dust[i]; if (!p.out && t >= p.wait) { p.out = true; p.card.o.clearRect(p.lx - .5, p.ly - .5, p.s + 1, p.s + 1); } }
  pictures.forEach(function (c) { g.drawImage(c.off, c.x, c.y, c.w, c.h); });
  for (var j = 0; j < dust.length; j++) {
    var q = dust[j], e = (t - q.wait) / 1000; if (e < 0) { alive++; continue; }
    var a = 1 - e / q.life; if (a <= 0) continue; alive++;
    g.fillStyle = (e < .12 ? q.c : q.f) + a.toFixed(3) + ')';
    g.fillRect(q.x + q.vx * e + Math.sin(q.seed + e * 4) * 10 * e, q.y + q.vy * e - 24 * e * e, q.s * (0.6 + a * .4), q.s * (0.6 + a * .4));
  }
  if (alive) requestAnimationFrame(frame); else done();
}
function snap(input) {
  if (phase !== 'idle') return;
  var list = cards(input.ids && input.ids.length ? input.ids : ctx.selection);
  if (!list.length) return idle();
  if (!lienzo.view || ctx.extension.permissions.indexOf('view') < 0) { hint.textContent = 'Allow Snap to see the view first (the chip above has Allow).'; return; }
  phase = 'dust'; hint.style.display = 'none'; job = input;
  lienzo.view.get().then(function (view) {
    list = list.filter(function (b) { return view.rects[b.id]; });
    if (!list.length) return idle();
    var ids = list.map(function (b) { return b.id; });
    var shot = lienzo.view.canSnapshot ? lienzo.view.snapshot(ids).catch(function () { return null; }) : Promise.resolve(null);
    return shot.then(function (s) { return (s ? load(s.url) : Promise.resolve(null)).then(function (img) {
      dust = []; pictures = []; list.forEach(function (b) { grains(view.rects[b.id], img, s && s.rect, b); });
      var x0 = Infinity, y0 = Infinity, x1 = -Infinity, y1 = -Infinity;
      ids.forEach(function (id) { var r = view.rects[id]; x0 = Math.min(x0, r.x); y0 = Math.min(y0, r.y); x1 = Math.max(x1, r.x + r.width); y1 = Math.max(y1, r.y + r.height); });
      at = { x: (x0 + x1) / 2, y: (y0 + y1) / 2 }; snapped = ids;
      // Hidden only on this screen, never saved; back by themselves after a minute, or when Snap closes.
      return lienzo.hide(ids, { ms: 60000 }).then(function () { t0 = performance.now(); requestAnimationFrame(frame); });
    }); });
  }).catch(function (err) { phase = 'idle'; hint.textContent = err.message; hint.style.display = 'block'; });
}
function done() {
  pictures = []; dust = []; g.clearRect(0, 0, W, H); var input = job; job = {};
  if (input.delete === true) return remove();
  if (input.delete === false) return restore();
  phase = 'ask'; var n = snapped.length;
  document.getElementById('title').textContent = n === 1 ? 'One card turned to dust' : n + ' cards turned to dust';
  var can = ctx.extension.permissions.indexOf('edit') >= 0;
  document.getElementById('text').textContent = can ? 'Delete them for good (Undo still works), or bring them back.' : 'Snap may not change the canvas, so they can only come back.';
  del.style.display = can ? '' : 'none';
  ask.style.left = Math.max(12, Math.min(W - 276, at.x - 132)) + 'px'; ask.style.top = Math.max(12, Math.min(H - 140, at.y - 50)) + 'px'; ask.style.display = 'block';
  // The overlay lets clicks through to the canvas; while it asks, it takes them.
  lienzo.ui.capturePointer(true); del.focus();
}
function restore() { lienzo.show(snapped).then(idle); }
function remove() {
  var n = snapped.length;
  lienzo.edit(snapped.map(function (id) { return { type: 'block.delete', id: id }; }), n === 1 ? 'Snap a card' : 'Snap ' + n + ' cards')
    .then(function () { return lienzo.show(snapped); }, function (err) { document.getElementById('text').textContent = err.message; return lienzo.show(snapped); })
    .then(idle);
}
back.onclick = restore; del.onclick = remove;
</script>
```

## A complete example

Title Case: the whole extension, ready to save or import.

This is a complete, small extension. It reads the selection, shows how many cards are selected, and rewrites their titles in one undoable step. It uses the theme's colours so it reads well in light and dark, and it brings its own Help page.

### Ask your agent

- “Save the Title Case example from Lienzo Help as an extension.”

### The page (html)
```html
<style>body{margin:0;padding:12px;font:13px system-ui,sans-serif}button{font:inherit;padding:6px 12px;border-radius:6px;border:1px solid;cursor:pointer}button:disabled{opacity:.5;cursor:default}</style>
<p id="info">Select some cards.</p>
<button id="go" disabled>Title Case the titles</button>
<script data-lienzo="actions">
// The work, once: the button below runs it, and so can an agent (canvas_extension_run), headless, without this page.
function titleCase(t) { return t.replace(/\b\w/g, function (c) { return c.toUpperCase(); }); }
lienzo.action('titleCase', function (input, c) {
  var ids = input.ids || c.selection;
  var ops = c.document.blocks.filter(function (b) { return ids.indexOf(b.id) >= 0 && titleCase(b.title) !== b.title; })
    .slice(0, 200).map(function (b) { return { type: 'block.update', id: b.id, patch: { title: titleCase(b.title) } }; });
  if (!ops.length) return { changed: 0 };
  return lienzo.edit(ops, 'Title Case').then(function () { return { changed: ops.length }; });
});
</script>
<script>
var info = document.getElementById('info'), go = document.getElementById('go');
lienzo.onContext(function (c) {
  var k = c.theme.colors, n = c.document.blocks.filter(function (b) { return c.selection.indexOf(b.id) >= 0; }).length;
  document.body.style.background = k.surface; document.body.style.color = k.foreground;
  go.style.background = k.accent; go.style.color = k.background; go.style.borderColor = k.accent;
  info.textContent = n ? n + ' selected' : 'Select some cards.';
  go.disabled = !n;
});
go.onclick = function () {
  lienzo.run('titleCase', {}).then(function (r) { info.textContent = r.changed ? 'Done. Undo brings the old titles back.' : 'They are in Title Case already.'; }, function (e) { info.textContent = e.message; });
};
</script>
```

### The file to share
Export writes the extension inside the file container. Its id is the file's id and a dot:
```json
{
  "format": "paseo-canvas-pack",
  "version": 1,
  "id": "title-case",
  "name": "Title Case",
  "description": "Gives the selected cards titles in Title Case.",
  "blockTypes": [],
  "templates": [],
  "documents": [],
  "extensions": [
    {
      "id": "title-case.title-case",
      "kind": "tool",
      "api": 1,
      "name": "Title Case",
      "description": "Gives the selected cards titles in Title Case.",
      "icon": "CaseSensitive",
      "permissions": [
        "edit"
      ],
      "html": "…the page above…",
      "docs": "…its Help page…",
      "actions": [
        {
          "name": "titleCase",
          "description": "Rewrites card titles in Title Case, in one undoable edit. Without ids it works on the cards the person selected.",
          "input": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
              "ids": {
                "type": "array",
                "items": {
                  "type": "string"
                },
                "maxItems": 200,
                "description": "The cards to change. Default: the person's selection."
              }
            }
          },
          "returns": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
              "changed": {
                "type": "integer",
                "description": "How many titles changed."
              }
            }
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```
